subject: Priv infra IaC decomposition + QA sprint: rollback policy & network harden review
messages:
From: Sanjay Ramesh <sanjay.ramesh@edgecorp.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Priv infra handoff: decomposing monolithic TF module + network hardening

Marcus —

Thanks for taking this on. We finished an initial internal audit and attached the auto-scan report (edgecorp_priv-iac-scan.pdf). The short version: our current terraform module for the private stack is ~6k LOC, mixes VPC, routing, firewall policies and node-provisioning, and it's blocking our compliance review. We need to split the module into clear responsibilities (vpc/networking, cluster/compute, security policies) and harden the default network policies for the on-prem appliance.

High level asks:
- A decomposition plan that keeps rollout atomic (we can't have windows where routes are partial).
- A tested rollback plan for failed module rollouts (we saw a bad change break peering last week).
- CI gating: a lightweight QA sprint runbook that can be executed by our engineers (and by your team during joint testing).

Can you propose a checklist and an initial schedule for a short QA sprint? We prefer next week if you have capacity.

Attached: edgecorp_priv-iac-scan.pdf

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Ramesh
Head of Platform Ops, EdgeCorp Systems

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Ramesh <sanjay.ramesh@edgecorp.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priv infra handoff: decomposing monolithic TF module + network hardening

Sanjay —

Appreciate the report, and sorry to hear about the peering incident. I skimmed the scan: a lot of policy drift and some overly permissive default CIDR rules. We can run a focused QA sprint next Tue–Thu (10/06–10/08).

Initial proposal (high level):
1) Decomposition plan (we'll author PRs to split modules):
   - vpc/peering (static resources, peerings, route tables)
   - netpol/firewalls (calico/network policies + firewall appliance rules)
   - compute & bootstrap (ansible playbooks, node labels, init hooks)
2) Rollback policy: immutable change windows + migration songs: anchor statefile + preflight diff + automated revert PRs. I'll attach a draft workflow (proposed-rollback-workflow.md).
3) CI gating & QA sprint runbook: smoke tests (connectivity matrix), policy regression tests (deny-by-default scenarios), staged canary on a replica VPC.

Can I loop in Irene (networking) and Hannah (CI/CD) to refine the checklist and own the runbook tasks? If that works, we'll open a GH meta-issue and a single PR per module split so change sets are reviewable and revertable.

Next steps:
- I propose a 45-minute sync tomorrow to align on scope and the canary plan.
- I'll post the PR skeletons and the rollback workflow to the repo tonight.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sanjay Ramesh <sanjay.ramesh@edgecorp.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priv infra handoff: decomposing monolithic TF module + network hardening

Thanks for the context. Quick notes from networking POV:
- Splitting modules is the right move; ensure the vpc/peering module owns route propagation and does NOT mutate firewall rules. Firewall rules should be an explicit netpol module so changes are auditable.
- For peering rollbacks: we should create a compatibility layer in TF (resource_aliasing + lifecycle ignore_changes) so peering updates are staged before route table flips. That avoids transient blackholes.
- For QA: we need a connectivity matrix CSV that enumerates critical flows (control-plane, KV-store replication, telemetry egress). I'll draft that and add it to the GH meta-issue.

One question for EdgeCorp: do you have a secondary management path (out-of-band) to break peering safely? If not, our canary will run in a read-only replica to minimize blast radius.

Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Ramesh <sanjay.ramesh@edgecorp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Priv infra handoff: decomposing monolithic TF module + network hardening

Irene / Marcus —

We do not have a dedicated out-of-band path today; ops-support is on copy. We can provision a jump-host but it will take 48 hours. For the short sprint, a read-only replica plan is safest.

Action items from our side: provisioning a replica VPC + test endpoints (should be ready by 10/06 morning). We'll also upload the inventory matrix to the Drive link you shared once it's complete.

Sanjay

Quick sync notes and planner (from today's call):

- Sprint window: 2026-10-06 09:00 PT — 2026-10-08 17:00 PT (three-day focused QA and PR landings).
- Owners:
  * vpc/peering decomposition: Irene (owner) — open PRs: priv-iac#482 (vpc split), priv-iac#483 (peerings).
  * netpol/firewall harden: Marcus + EdgeCorp ops (joint) — netpol-diff.patch attached.
  * rollback automation: Hannah (owner) — will add a GitHub Actions workflow that creates revert PRs on failed canary jobs.
- CI gating: mandatory smoke + policy regression for any PR touching netpol or routing. Jobs run in parallel in GH Actions; failure blocks merge.
- Rollback playbook: see attached proposed-rollback-workflow.md — contains a fast path (PR revert) and a slow path (manual state rollback via statefile snapshot + apply).
- Testing approach: staged canary on replica VPC, then a single customer-facing cut at low-traffic hour with a 30-minute observation window. If anomalies > threshold, auto-revert.

Open questions:
1) EdgeCorp: are you comfortable with a 30-minute observation window for cutover?
2) Dev: can you confirm Ansible bootstrap tasks are idempotent under partial route state?

Next steps: I'll land the PR skeletons tonight and ping the GH PRs. Please comment directly on the PRs to keep review history centralized.

Attachments in thread: edgecorp_priv-iac-scan.pdf, proposed-rollback-workflow.md, netpol-diff.patch

Thanks all — looking forward to the sprint.

—Marcus
